---
title: "Cohort shifts by phase"
subtitle: "Each phase against the follicular phase, within the same participants. Interval 2022, 37–42 participants per cell."
---

Positive means higher than on the participant's own follicular days. Paired mean differences with 95 % bias-corrected bootstrap intervals over 5,000 participant resamples ([methods](methods.qmd)). In the same participants the luteal phase moves five of the six device metrics (sleep duration does not change); menses moves the symptoms. These contrasts agree in direction with published wearable studies ([Shilaih et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-01433-9); [Goodale et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.2196/13404); [Schmalenberger et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm8111946)); what is new here is their size, in native units with intervals, for this dataset.

![Shifts in native units with their bootstraps. Top: six device metrics, each on its own scale, three contrasts per metric. Bottom: eleven diary symptoms in points on their 0–5 scale, one panel per contrast. Half-violin: the bootstrap distribution of the paired mean difference over 5,000 participant resamples; dot and bar: the estimate with its 95 % BCa interval; the number is the estimate.](figures/P1_phenovector_forest.png)

## Standardized, to compare across metrics

Hedges' g uses the spread of participants' phase means as its unit, so a consistent 3 bpm shift against baselines that differ by 7 bpm between people scores lower than a one-point symptom shift against baselines that differ by less than a point. Use it to compare cells, not to size an effect.

![Whorlmap of Hedges' g. Each cell spirals its 5,000 bootstrap values from the tail nearest zero (outer ring) to the far tail (centre), 2.5 % trimmed at each end, so a coloured outer ring means the 95 % interval excludes zero. Colour range ±2, set by the widest cell. Rows ordered within each family by its strongest contrast.](figures/P2_phenovector_whorlmap.png)

![The same g with its bootstrap as half-violins, families by contrasts. Each family row has its own scale.](figures/P4_phenovector_forest_g.png)

![Do two phase contrasts move the same features? One dot per feature. The fertile-window and luteal vectors point the same way; menses is its own direction. Descriptive: features are not independent.](figures/P3_vector_pairs.png)

## Read with

- **Reference phase.** The app's "Follicular" label is the late-follicular phase, from the last day of flow to the first day of the fertile window, the same definition the dataset's papers use. In this release it is short (median 6 labelled days, against 7.7–11 days in the papers), and the cohort and estimators differ, so agreement with the papers is same-direction, not replication.
- **Open cycles included.** Days in cycles that never closed count towards their labelled phase. Restricted to closed cycles, the luteal contrasts agree for resting heart rate (+3.0 bpm), temperature (+0.28 °C), glucose (+0.21 mmol/L) and breathing rate (+0.53 /min); HRV is smaller there (−2.5 ms against −3.9), so its size depends on that choice.
- **Multiplicity.** 51 cells, no adjustment. 30 exclude zero; two or three would by chance. Symptom cells are strongly correlated with each other.
- **Not blind.** Participants saw the app's phase predictions while reporting symptoms.
- **Data handling.** 782 of 3,698 resting-heart-rate days were coded 0 and treated as missing; two participants' glucose was converted from mg/dL; 16 of 3,258 temperature nights were dropped as artefacts.

Table: [`tables/cohort_phenovector.csv`](tables/cohort_phenovector.csv), 51 rows, no identifiers.
